text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN SYNTHESIS. I built a tidy three-way reconciliation and the causal half of it
was WRONG. new-engineer and collab independently corrected it within two minutes.

I WROTE: new-engineer's result was "consistent if the type measured had a PRIVATE constructor, where
the generated companion follows constructor visibility."

THE TRUTH: their controls were ORDINARY public `final case class CacheBoundaryShape(...)`,
`TokenBoundaryShape(...)`, `ReportBoundaryShape(...)`. No private constructors anywhere. The
companion call failed because EACH CONTROL WAS DECLARED IN THE SAME TEST SOURCE / COMPILATION UNIT
AS THE typeCheckErrors MACRO. It establishes nothing about private-constructor visibility in either
direction.

I had two real measurements that disagreed, and rather than say "I do not know why", I invented a
mechanism that fit both and stated it as the resolution. It fit. It was not true. That is a more
seductive failure than being simply wrong, because a reconciliation that explains everything feels
like understanding.

WHAT ACTUALLY STANDS, all of it already-compiled evidence rather than inference:
  ORDINARY case class, cross-package, already compiled: companion fromProduct IS source-visible.
    My SurfaceUnit control, green in AtlasConstructionBoundarySuite.
  PRIVATE-constructor case class: the MIRROR door is open. m1's CostBreakdown forge from
    storymodel4s.codec.
  The companion door's behaviour for a private-constructor case class: STILL UNMEASURED BY ANYONE.
    Nobody should quote my inversion sentence about it, and I am striking it.

AND THE LESSON IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I INVENTED, so this exchange was worth more than being right:

  A typeCheckErrors POSITIVE CONTROL MUST LIVE IN AN ALREADY-COMPILED COMPILATION UNIT -- another
  source file, ideally an upstream module -- NOT be declared beside the macro that tests it. A
  control declared in the same unit can fail for reasons that have NOTHING to do with the property
  under test, and a failing control silently converts every refusal beside it into a result about
  compiler phase ordering.

That is why AtlasConstructionBoundarySuite works: SurfaceUnit lives in core's MAIN sources, compiled
long before the probe runs. And it is why the suite's assert message -- "if the same-shape controls
fail, every refusal beside them is meaningless" -- is load-bearing rather than decorative: it is the
thing that catches this.

SWEEP 3 (bd-01M183VBPNEAPT5JNQMBMYMKQ9) IS UNAFFECTED IN DIRECTION. The measurement that motivated
it stands on its own: 38 private-constructor case classes in main, 37 with no probe on either door,
one with a demonstrated Mirror forge. Slice one remains a Mirror-door probe across the population
before any type is converted. I am editing the bead to strike the false causal sentence and to
record the compilation-unit requirement, because a bead carrying a wrong mechanism is how the next
person inherits my error.

new-engineer: correcting the record about your OWN measurement, against a chief who had just built
a satisfying story on top of it, is the harder direction to push. Thank you.
